hypertension.analogy: Like water pushing too hard against the walls of a garden hose.

tachycardia.plain: A faster than normal heart rate

bradycardia.plain: A slower than normal heart rate

arrhythmia.plain: An irregular heartbeat: too fast, too slow, or uneven

atrial fibrillation.plain: A common irregular heartbeat where the upper chambers of the heart quiver instead of beating steadily

myocardial infarction.plain: A heart attack: part of the heart muscle is damaged because its blood flow was blocked

angina.plain: Chest pain or pressure when the heart muscle is not getting enough blood
angina.swap: chest pain from reduced blood flow to the heart (angina)

murmur.plain: An extra or unusual sound heard during a heartbeat. Often harmless, but sometimes points to a valve problem

hyperlipidemia.plain: High levels of fats, like cholesterol, in the blood

cholesterol.plain: A waxy, fat-like substance in the blood. Too much of some types can build up inside arteries

edema.plain: Swelling caused by extra fluid trapped in body tissue

ischemia.plain: Not enough blood flow to part of the body

thrombosis.plain: A blood clot forming inside a blood vessel
thrombosis.swap: blood clot in a blood vessel (thrombosis)

embolism.plain: A blockage caused by a clot or other material traveling through the bloodstream

stenosis.plain: Narrowing of a passage in the body, such as a blood vessel or heart valve

aneurysm.plain: A bulge in the wall of a blood vessel that can weaken and may burst
aneurysm.swap: bulge in a blood vessel wall (aneurysm)

syncope.plain: Fainting: a short loss of consciousness, often from reduced blood flow to the brain

anemia.plain: A lower than normal level of healthy red blood cells

leukocytes.plain: White blood cells, the cells that fight infection
leukocytes.analogy: Think of them as your body's security team.

erythrocytes.plain: Red blood cells, the cells that carry oxygen around the body

platelets.plain: Tiny blood cells that help your blood clot

leukocytosis.plain: A higher than normal number of white blood cells, which can be a sign of infection or inflammation

leukopenia.plain: A lower than normal number of white blood cells

thrombocytopenia.plain: A lower than normal number of platelets, which can make bleeding or bruising easier

hemoglobin.plain: The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen
hemoglobin.swap: hemoglobin (the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells)

hematocrit.plain: The percentage of your blood that is made up of red blood cells
hematocrit.swap: hematocrit (the share of blood made of red blood cells)

creatinine.plain: A waste product from muscles. The level in your blood helps show how well your kidneys are working

sepsis.plain: A life-threatening reaction to an infection, where the body's response starts damaging its own organs

hyperkalemia.plain: Higher than normal potassium in the blood

hypokalemia.plain: Lower than normal potassium in the blood

hypernatremia.plain: Higher than normal sodium in the blood

hyponatremia.plain: Lower than normal sodium in the blood

diabetes mellitus.plain: A condition where the body cannot properly control the level of sugar in the blood

insulin.plain: A hormone that helps sugar move from the blood into the body's cells to be used for energy
insulin.analogy: Like a key that unlocks the door of each cell so sugar can get in.
insulin.swap: insulin (a hormone that moves sugar into cells)

hypothyroidism.plain: An underactive thyroid gland that does not make enough thyroid hormone

hyperthyroidism.plain: An overactive thyroid gland that makes too much thyroid hormone

HbA1c.plain: A blood test showing your average blood sugar over the past 2 to 3 months
HbA1c.swap: A1c (average blood sugar over 2 to 3 months)

A1c.plain: A blood test showing your average blood sugar over the past 2 to 3 months
A1c.swap: A1c (average blood sugar over 2 to 3 months)

diagnosis.plain: The name doctors give to the condition that is causing your symptoms

benign.plain: Not cancer; not harmful in the way cancer is

malignant.plain: Cancerous; able to grow into nearby tissue and spread

metastasis.plain: Cancer spreading from where it started to other parts of the body
metastasis.swap: spread of cancer to other body parts (metastasis)

tumor.plain: An abnormal lump or mass of tissue. It can be benign or malignant

lesion.plain: An area of tissue that is abnormal because of injury or disease

carcinoma.plain: A type of cancer that starts in the skin or in the tissue lining organs

biopsy.plain: Removing a small sample of tissue so it can be examined in a lab

remission.plain: When signs and symptoms of a disease have decreased or disappeared
remission.swap: period with little or no sign of disease

prognosis.plain: The likely outcome or course of a disease

etiology.plain: The cause of a disease or condition

differential diagnosis.plain: A list of possible conditions that could explain the symptoms, which the doctor narrows down with tests

idiopathic.analogy: Doctors use this when they can see what is happening but not why.

within normal limits.plain: The result is in the expected healthy range

auscultation.plain: Listening to the heart, lungs, or gut with a stethoscope

contraindicated.plain: Not recommended because it could cause harm in this situation
contraindicated.swap: not recommended because it could cause harm

dyspnea.plain: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing

hypoxia.plain: Low oxygen levels in the body's tissues

pneumonia.plain: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs

asthma.plain: A condition where the airways swell and narrow, making it harder to breathe
asthma.swap: asthma (a condition that narrows the airways)

bronchitis.plain: Inflammation of the airways that carry air into the lungs

effusion.plain: Extra fluid that has collected around an organ or in a joint, such as around the lungs

cyanosis.plain: A bluish color of the skin or lips, which can mean low oxygen

COPD.plain: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a long-term lung disease that makes breathing hard (includes emphysema and chronic bronchitis)

SpO2.plain: Blood oxygen level, usually measured by a small sensor clipped to a finger

jaundice.plain: Yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes, often linked to liver or blood problems
jaundice.swap: yellowing of the skin and eyes

reflux.plain: Stomach acid flowing back up into the esophagus (the tube from the mouth to the stomach)

dialysis.plain: A treatment that does the kidneys' job of filtering waste from the blood

GERD.plain: Gastroesophageal reflux disease: frequent acid reflux that can irritate the esophagus

UTI.plain: Urinary tract infection: an infection in the bladder, kidneys, or the tubes between them

inflammation.plain: The body's response to injury or infection, often causing redness, swelling, heat, and pain

neuropathy.plain: Nerve damage that can cause numbness, tingling, or pain

vertigo.plain: A feeling that you or the room is spinning

seizure.plain: A sudden burst of abnormal electrical activity in the brain
seizure.swap: seizure (a sudden burst of abnormal brain activity)

arthritis.plain: Inflammation of the joints, causing pain and stiffness

osteoporosis.plain: A condition where bones become weak and brittle

laceration.plain: A cut or tear in the skin

lethargy.plain: Unusual tiredness or lack of energy

malaise.plain: A general feeling of being unwell

anaphylaxis.plain: A severe, life-threatening allergic reaction that needs emergency care

CBC.plain: Complete blood count: a common blood test that measures red cells, white cells, and platelets
CBC.swap: complete blood count (a common blood test)

BMP.plain: Basic metabolic panel: a blood test checking sugar, salts, and kidney function

CMP.plain: Comprehensive metabolic panel: a blood test that checks sugar, salts, kidney function, and liver function

BUN.plain: Blood urea nitrogen: a blood test that helps show how well the kidneys are working

ECG.plain: Electrocardiogram: a test that records the heart's electrical activity

EKG.plain: Electrocardiogram: a test that records the heart's electrical activity

MRI.plain: Magnetic resonance imaging: detailed pictures of the inside of the body made with magnets, no radiation

CT.plain: Computed tomography: a scan that uses many X-ray images to make detailed pictures of the inside of the body

IV.plain: Intravenous: given directly into a vein

BID.plain: Twice a day (used in medication instructions)

TID.plain: Three times a day (used in medication instructions)

NPO.plain: Nothing by mouth: no food or drink

antibiotic.plain: A medicine that kills bacteria or stops them from growing. It does not work on viruses

anticoagulant.plain: A blood thinner: a medicine that makes blood clot more slowly

diuretic.plain: A medicine that helps the body get rid of extra water and salt through urine, sometimes called a water pill

antihypertensive.plain: A medicine that lowers blood pressure

corticosteroid.plain: A medicine that reduces inflammation and calms the immune system

prophylaxis.plain: Treatment given to prevent a disease before it happens

cardiovascular.plain: Related to the heart and blood vessels

palpitations.plain: The feeling that your heart is racing, pounding, skipping a beat, or fluttering
palpitations.swap: awareness of a racing or pounding heartbeat

perfusion.plain: The flow of blood through the body's tissues and organs

heart failure.plain: A condition where the heart cannot pump blood as well as the body needs. It does not mean the heart has stopped
heart failure.swap: heart failure (the heart isn't pumping well enough)

orthostatic.plain: Related to standing up. For example, orthostatic dizziness is lightheadedness when you stand

hematoma.plain: A collection of blood outside blood vessels, often felt as a bruise-like lump

proteinuria.plain: Too much protein in the urine, which can be a sign of kidney problems

polyuria.plain: Passing larger than normal amounts of urine

melena.plain: Black, tar-like stool, which can be a sign of bleeding in the upper digestive tract

dyspepsia.plain: Indigestion: discomfort or pain in the upper belly after eating

glomerulonephritis.plain: Inflammation of the glomeruli, the tiny filters inside the kidneys
glomerulonephritis.analogy: Think of the kidney's filters becoming irritated and swollen.
glomerulonephritis.swap: inflammation of the kidneys' tiny filters (glomerulonephritis)

renal insufficiency.plain: The kidneys are not working as well as they should

kidney failure.plain: The kidneys can no longer filter waste from the blood well enough on their own

pyelonephritis.plain: A kidney infection, usually spread from the bladder

cystitis.plain: Inflammation of the bladder, often from an infection

appendicitis.plain: Inflammation of the appendix, a small pouch attached to the large intestine. It often needs urgent care

diverticulitis.plain: Inflamed or infected small pouches in the wall of the colon
diverticulitis.swap: inflamed pouches in the colon wall (diverticulitis)

gastroenteritis.plain: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines, often called stomach flu

gastrointestinal.plain: Related to the stomach and intestines

pharyngeal.plain: Related to the pharynx, which is the throat

pharyngitis.plain: Inflammation of the throat, commonly called a sore throat

tonsillitis.plain: Inflammation of the tonsils, the two lumps of tissue at the back of the throat

sinusitis.plain: Inflammation of the sinuses, the air spaces in the bones around the nose

hemoptysis.plain: Coughing up blood from the lungs or airways

conjunctivitis.plain: Inflammation of the thin layer covering the white of the eye, often called pink eye

glaucoma.plain: A group of eye conditions that damage the optic nerve, often from high pressure inside the eye
glaucoma.swap: eye disease that damages the optic nerve (glaucoma)

cataract.plain: Clouding of the eye's lens that makes vision blurry

meningitis.plain: Inflammation of the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, usually from an infection. It needs urgent care
meningitis.swap: inflammation of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord (meningitis)

cellulitis.plain: A bacterial infection of the skin and the tissue just beneath it

osteoarthritis.plain: The most common type of arthritis, caused by wear and tear on the joints

tendinitis.plain: Inflammation of a tendon, the cord that attaches muscle to bone

bursitis.plain: Inflammation of a bursa, a small fluid-filled cushion near a joint

atrophy.plain: Wasting away or shrinking of body tissue or an organ

hypertrophy.plain: Enlargement of an organ or tissue because its cells have grown larger

sequelae.plain: Lasting effects left after a disease or injury

comorbidity.plain: Another health condition a person has at the same time as the main one
comorbidity.swap: another health condition at the same time

exacerbation.plain: A flare-up: symptoms getting suddenly worse

neurological.plain: Related to the brain, spinal cord, and nerves

musculoskeletal.plain: Related to the muscles and bones

systemic.plain: Affecting the whole body rather than one part

insufficiency.plain: An organ or system is not working as well as it should

melanoma.plain: A serious type of skin cancer that starts in the cells that make skin color

lymphoma.plain: Cancer that starts in the lymph system, part of the body's infection-fighting network

leukemia.plain: Cancer of the blood-forming tissues, such as the bone marrow

proximal.plain: Closer to the center of the body or to where something starts
proximal.swap: closer to the center of the body

distal.plain: Farther from the center of the body or from where something starts
distal.swap: farther from the center of the body

anterior.plain: Toward the front of the body

posterior.plain: Toward the back of the body

lateral.plain: Toward the side of the body

acute appendicitis.plain: Sudden inflammation of the appendix, a small pouch attached to the large intestine. It usually needs urgent care
acute appendicitis.swap: sudden inflammation of the appendix (acute appendicitis)

chronic kidney disease.plain: Long-term, slowly worsening loss of kidney function

urinary tract infection.plain: An infection in the bladder, kidneys, or the tubes between them

type 2 diabetes.plain: A type of diabetes where the body does not use insulin well, so blood sugar runs high

type 1 diabetes.plain: A type of diabetes where the body makes little or no insulin

congestive heart failure.plain: Heart failure that has caused fluid to build up in the lungs or other parts of the body

deep vein thrombosis.plain: A blood clot in a deep vein, usually in the leg
deep vein thrombosis.swap: blood clot in a deep vein (deep vein thrombosis)

tenderness.plain: Pain when an area is touched or pressed

guarding.plain: Tightening of the belly muscles when the belly is touched, usually to protect a painful area
guarding.swap: tightening of belly muscles to protect a sore spot

rebound tenderness.plain: Pain that gets worse when pressure on the belly is quickly let go
rebound tenderness.swap: pain that gets worse when pressure is released

mcburney's point.plain: A spot in the lower right belly where appendicitis pain is often felt
mcburney's point.swap: McBurney's point (the lower right belly spot where appendicitis often hurts)

neutrophils.plain: The most common white blood cell. They are first responders against infection, especially bacterial infection
neutrophils.swap: neutrophils (white blood cells that fight infection)

neutrophilia.plain: A higher than normal number of neutrophils, a type of white blood cell

neutrophilic predominance.plain: Neutrophils make up the largest share of the white blood cells

distension.plain: Swelling or stretching of the belly or another body part, often from gas or fluid

palpable.plain: Able to be felt by touch

malignant melanoma.plain: A serious type of skin cancer that starts in the cells that make skin color

malignant tumor.plain: A cancerous lump of tissue that can grow into nearby tissue and spread

benign tumor.plain: A lump of tissue that is not cancer

localized tenderness.plain: Pain when one specific spot is touched or pressed
localized tenderness.swap: pain in one spot when touched

voluntary guarding.plain: The patient tightens their belly muscles on purpose to protect a painful area
voluntary guarding.swap: tensing the belly muscles on purpose to protect a sore spot
